column4: Visit note | 2025-01-05 10:00 AM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Kamal Alam, 54, male. Mr. Alam presents with significant stiffness in his right shoulder, reporting that he cannot lift his arm or reach behind his back. He works as a software developer. The issue started after weeks of keeping the arm still after a sprain in Banani. He has a history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus, which is a known predisposing factor. He denies any recent trauma, neck pain, or numbness in his hand. On examination: BP 120/82 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 73 kg. Active and passive range of motion of the glenohumeral joint is severely restricted in all planes, and shoulder lifts only to 95 degrees. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 11:30 AM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Popy Gazi, 77, female. Mrs. Gazi complains of tightness in her chest when walking quickly or climbing stairs, accompanied by shortness of breath during physical effort. She works as a tailor. The symptoms first started while carrying shopping bags uphill in Rampura. She has no known comorbidities. There is no history of chest pain at rest, palpitations, or ankle swelling. On examination: BP 138/87 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 54 kg. Her chest is clear on auscultation, and heart sounds are normal. Assessment: Stable angina. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid heavy exertion until review, walk 20 minutes daily on flat ground, and stop smoking. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and fasting lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 02:00 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Zakia Mahmud, 75, female. Mrs. Mahmud presents after being alerted to a high reading on a pharmacy machine, though she has no other major complaints apart from occasional dizziness. She is a madrasa teacher. This elevated reading was first found during a free health camp in Bashundhara. She has no chronic medical conditions. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or headache. On examination: BP 163/96 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 57 kg. Cardiovascular examination is otherwise unremarkable with normal heart sounds. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 03:00 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Sohel Kabir, 80, male. Mr. Kabir presents complaining of a constant feeling of thirst, minor cuts that heal very slowly, and needing to pass urine frequently. He is a shopkeeper. These symptoms were noticed after a relative in Tejgaon was diagnosed and advised testing. His comorbidities include Essential hypertension. He denies any burning sensation during urination, fever, or vision changes. On examination: fasting glucose 9.3 mmol/L, BP 138/95 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 74 kg. Sensation in both feet is intact. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly 30 minutes five days a week, check fasting sugar twice weekly, and check the feet daily. Follow-up in 3 months with HbA1c.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 03:00 PM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Sraboni Das, 39, female. Ms. Das presents with severe vaginal itching and a thick, white discharge. She works as an electrician. She mentions that this started after using a new scented soap bought in Chattogram. She has a known history of Bronchial asthma. She denies pelvic pain, dysuria, or fever. On examination: random blood glucose 5.4 mmol/L, BP 125/70 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 85 kg. Gynecological inspection reveals vulvovaginal erythema and thick curd-like discharge. Assessment: Vulvovaginal candidiasis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to wear cotton underwear, avoid scented soaps, and keep the area dry. Follow-up in 2 weeks if it does not clear.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 03:30 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Jannatul Bepari, 34, female. Mrs. Bepari reports experiencing a racing heart, shaky hands, and unintentional weight loss despite having a good appetite. She is a tailor. The symptoms began after a stressful family event in Bashundhara. She has a comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. She denies any heat intolerance, neck swelling, or changes in vision. On examination: pulse 112 bpm, BP 136/84 mmHg, weight 73 kg. Fine tremors are observed in both outstretched hands, and there is mild tachycardia. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee, and rest when the heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 03:30 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Sadia Alam, 63, female. Mrs. Alam presents complaining of watery, itchy eyes and nasal congestion that worsen significantly when exposed to dust. She is a madrasa teacher. Her symptoms have been worse since road construction began near home in Sirajganj. She has no other medical conditions. She denies fever, facial pain, or sore throat. On examination: about 5 sneezing fits a day, BP 134/81 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 72 kg. Nasal examination shows pale, boggy turbinates with clear watery discharge. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 04:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Nazma Sultana, 74, female. Mrs. Sultana presents with a long history of smoking, noting that her breathlessness has been significantly worse for several days, accompanied by more sputum production than usual. She is a retired civil servant. The symptoms worsened during the dusty dry season in Rampura. She has no other chronic comorbidities. She denies chest pain, high fever, or leg swelling. On examination: SpO2 91%, BP 136/70 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 55 kg. Chest auscultation reveals bilateral wheeze and prolonged expiration. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 04:00 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Shathi Mollah, 48, female. Mrs. Mollah reports vaginal soreness and a thick, white discharge. She works as a fisherman. The symptoms started after using a new scented soap bought in Dhanmondi. There are no known comorbidities. She denies pelvic pain, dysuria, or abnormal bleeding. On examination: random blood glucose 7.7 mmol/L, BP 130/84 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 59 kg. Visual inspection shows vulvar erythema and classic cottage-cheese-like discharge. Assessment: Vulvovaginal candidiasis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to wear cotton underwear, avoid scented soaps, and keep the area dry. Follow-up in 2 weeks if it does not clear.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 04:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Ehsan Haque, 47, male. Mr. Haque presents complaining of chronic abdominal bloating and discomfort, reporting that his symptoms are worse with stress. He works as a restaurant cook. The issues began after a bout of food poisoning in Kamrangirchar. He has no other comorbidities. He denies weight loss, blood in stool, or nocturnal bowel movements. On examination: pain score 4/10, BP 129/80 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 54 kg. Abdomen is soft but mildly distended, with no focal tenderness or masses. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 04:30 PM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Faruk Hasan, 46, male. Mr. Hasan presents with cramping belly pain, bloating, and symptoms that worsen with stress. He reports an atypical presentation of urgent loose stools every morning with little pain. He works as a sales representative. His symptoms began after a bout of food poisoning in Narayanganj. He has no other comorbidities. He denies any blood in his stool, fever, or unexplained weight loss. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 112/71 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 72 kg. Abdomen is soft, slightly tympanitic, with mild generalized tenderness. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.
